title: Versioned control-plane rolling canary pipeline with programmable health probes
creator: Maya Patel
description: Deliver a robust, repeatable pipeline for rolling upgrades of the Private (VPC) control plane that supports semantic version tagging, staged canary traffic shifts, programmable health probes and automated rollback when predefined safety gates fail. The goal is to enable safe, low-friction control plane updates across customer VPCs with clear observability and minimal manual intervention. This ticket covers the orchestration glue (pipeline), a small reusable Terraform module set for canary rollout state, and the health probe DSL used to evaluate canary success. It does NOT include full-scale autoscaling changes or per-customer policy UI — those are separate tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Pipeline can deploy control-plane binary/container image tagged by semver (e.g., 1.18.2 -> 1.19.0-alpha) into a subset of target VPCs deterministically
A2: Health probe DSL evaluates 3 signal families (API liveness, RPC latency percentiles, and control-plane job success rate) and yields a pass/fail decision within configured windows
A3: Traffic shift can be configured to 5/20/50/100% stages with automated waits and metric checks between stages
A4: Pipeline rolls back automatically when any configured gate fails, and rollback is observable in console + annotated in pipeline run logs
A5: Terraform modules publish state to shared registry and support cross-account/statefile locking for private deployments
A6: End-to-end test harness (local emulated VPC) runs the pipeline and validates gating logic in CI without touching prod customers
tasks: T1: Design health probe DSL and define default probes for control-plane components
T2: Implement canary rollout pipeline in Flightdeck (or our CI runner) with staged traffic shift logic
T3: Create lightweight Terraform module (module.controlplane_canary) for marking canary pools and managing state
T4: Integrate KMS-backed secrets for image pulls and verify cross-account access patterns
T5: Implement rollback hooks and annotated GitHub Actions/PRs for manual intervention
T6: Add metrics thresholds and SLO checks wired into pipeline; connect to Console dashboards
T7: Author runbooks and incident playbooks for failed upgrades and partial rollbacks
T8: End-to-end CI job that runs upgrade against a sandbox VPC and asserts acceptance criteria
comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Patel: Created ticket after design sync with SRE and Product. Primary risk is false positives in health probes causing unnecessary rollbacks.

2025-02-19 Liam O'Connor: Spike complete. Implemented prototype probe DSL using Prometheus queries + synthetic request runner. Early results: latency P95 is noisy for small canaries; we should include moving-average smoothing and require trend-based checks.

2025-02-26 Design review: agreed to expose probe time windows and smoothing as pipeline config. Decided NOT to bake customer-specific thresholds into defaults — those live in per-customer override files.

2025-03-03 Engineering update: Terraform module scaffolding committed (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/PR-492). The module supports a 'canary_pool' resource and remote state outputs for the orchestrator to read.
2025-03-07 SRE note: Added circuit-breaker rule - if any control-plane replica restarts >3x within 10m during a stage, mark stage failed. Will be added to probe DSL as builtin rule.

2025-03-10 Liam O'Connor: Integration tests failing intermittently in CI; flakiness traced to emulated KV backend latency in sandbox. Mitigation: extend probe stabilization window in tests and add synthetic latency injection to validate robust gating.
2025-03-10 Maya Patel: Linking runbook draft and the design doc. Next steps: finalize thresholds, complete rollback choreography, and run cross-team dry-run with Solutions Engineering on 2025-03-18.
